title: Charles XII to the Rådet and his envoys, Bender, 26 April 1710 (catalogue 599): two copies in a Swedish homophonic nomenclator, key rebuilt by crib

steps.what: Ciphered troop list (fols. 73, 82) aligned with its clear draft (fol. 74); totals and officers' names fixed the first values, then the alphabetical structure of the table.
Key frozen, applied to pages never opened before: fol. 100 (German, 93% of words recognised) and fols. 78v-79r (96%); permuted and shuffled control keys at most 77-80%.
Both copies of the 26 April 1710 letter read and compared; 639 of 640 groups read.
Doubtful numbers checked blind on the image by Brice Dudout; the two copies cross-check (same words, sometimes clear in one copy and cipher in the other).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 638 tokens, 178 types, sv-modern order 4: reading -2.593 per letter; random keys -3.542 (z 7.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.327 (mean -2.354, z -14.6); annealer on the real text -2.24. Verdict: underdetermined.

Claude Opus 5.5 (PR review on merge): the not-attempted gap for the other letters of Nr. 670 moved to notes (outside this target); probable values counted (ten, not six); graded A. Repository slips noted for the contributor: key.tsv lacks 238, 473, 345 and 25 used by the reading, lists 1049 as wis? (reading wilkor), and has 160 = qi where decryption.txt writes qui.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.596; polyphony 0.002; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.24

texts.label: Charles XII, Bender, 26 April 1710: copies for the envoys (fol. 85) and for the Rådet (fols. 83-84)
texts.summary: A refugee at Bender, on Ottoman soil, since Poltava, Charles XII learns of the rout of the Danish army at Helsingborg. In a chancery letter whose sensitive passages are in cipher, he declares himself ready to make peace with Denmark under the mediation of England and the United Provinces, and gives the Council a “free hand” to negotiate and to conclude an armistice, “even for a whole year”. Two ciphered copies, received by the Swedish government of Bremen-Verden, are kept at Stade.

reading_review.note: Read both copies' group-by-group decryption against reading.md and translation.md: the number runs build Swedish sentences that join the clear text throughout. Weak passages: the Rådet copy's 'bo‹s-tag-are-i-212›t' (the one unread group, the clear before it poorly made out) and '‹slores› på ‹…› heelt års tid'; the (…) holes are in the fast clear hand, not in the cipher.

outcome.notes: The other cipher letters of Rep. 5a Nr. 670 are outside this target (catalogue 599, narrowed).

prior.where: Catalogue 599 open; no key in the file; web search 27 Oct 2026.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
